how the structure of fishing communities is influenced by fishing regulations.

fishing communities are not homogeneous, but rather are composed of different groups of boats skippers with specific fishing strategies that affect their social relations.

the fishing reserves have the potential to contribute to the sustainability of fishing communities, but only if the management of the reserve is based on a thorough knowledge of the social structure of the fishermen and their fishing strategies.

the social networks of the fishermen of the fishing reserve in the port of Chipiona and the recreational port of Sant Antoni de Potmany are similar in terms of their structure, but different in terms of their attitudes towards the incorporation of environmental uses and tourism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, despite the similarities in social network structure and the differences in attitudes towards environmental protection, the fishermen in the Fishing Reserve of Chipiona have a higher level of readiness to adopt environmental protection measures.
fishing communities are not only defined by the fishing grounds they share, but also by the social relations that emerge between them.

the fishing reserves can be an important contribution to modify the structure of economic incentives and social relations of fishermen.
